title: Xiang Yang Hong 33 Day 21: Chinese Research Vessel Maintains Record Pag-asa Presence; UNCLOS Note Verbale Silence Day 16 — PCG Sandy Cay Investigation Ongoing
detail: China's research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33, escorted by China Coast Guard vessels 5101 and 5309, maintained its unauthorized presence in Philippine maritime zones near Pag-asa (Thitu) Island for a 21st consecutive day on May 27, 2026 — as Beijing's diplomatic silence on the Philippines' UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale (filed May 11) extended to a 16th consecutive day without a formal Chinese Foreign Ministry response. The Xiang Yang Hong 33's record-setting unauthorized incursion — which began with marine scientific research in the Kalayaan Island Group on May 7, escalated to the territorial sea of Pag-asa Island by May 16-17, and included Chinese personnel landing on Sandy Cay 2 and Sandy Cay 3 — remained active with no indication of departure. The Philippine Coast Guard continued aerial surveillance operations and radio challenges against the vessel. The PCG's formal investigation into the Chinese personnel landing on Sandy Cay 2 and Sandy Cay 3 (within the 12 nm territorial sea of Pag-asa Island) remained ongoing, with no results published. The Philippines maintained its three-front West Philippine Sea standoff: (1) Xiang Yang Hong 33 near Pag-asa (Day 21, CCG escorts 5101 and 5309, Sandy Cay personnel landing investigation active, Day 16 of UNCLOS Article 246 note verbale silence — longest unanswered Philippine diplomatic instrument under the Marcos administration); (2) Scarborough Shoal — China's 'marine nature reserve' declaration disputed by DFA protest filed May 11, unanswered by Beijing; AFP weekly report confirmed 19 Chinese vessels (10 PLAN + 9 CCG) at Scarborough for May 19-25; (3) Second Thomas Shoal — BRP Sierra Madre marine garrison facing CCG blockade posture, AFP weekly count confirmed 9 vessels (1 PLAN + 8 CCG) at Ayungin Shoal for May 19-25. Total Chinese vessel presence of 36 across four WPS features for the May 19-25 period — up from 27 the prior week — confirmed by AFP's weekly monitoring report published May 26. China's Xinhua and Global Times continued to frame the Xiang Yang Hong 33's operations as legitimate scientific research and describe Philippine surveillance and documentation as 'harassment.' No kinetic engagement or new escalation was confirmed on May 27.
